*s s, si/gma or si=gma (both accents are found in codd.), to/, twentyfirst letter of the Etruscan abecedaria, IG 14.2420 , and prob. of the oldest Gr. alphabets (corresponding to the twenty-first Hebrew letter
shin <*>, Phoenician *w, Syria 6.103 ), but eighteenth of the Ion. alphabet: as numeral s/ =
200 , but s'
=
200 , 000 : a semi-vowel, Arist. Po. 1456b28 , cf. Pl. Tht. 203b . the oldest forms expressing this sound were *m (which is however the old eighteenth letter, q.v.), also *s and s; compared to a twisted curl, E. Fr. 382.7 , Theodect. 6 ; to a Scythian bow, Agatho 4 ; after this, but yet early, it took the shape of a semicircle <*>, whence Aeschrio ( Fr. 1 ) calls the new moon to\ kalo\n ou)ranou= ne/on si=gma: hence the orchestra is called to\ tou= qea/trou si=gma, Phot., AB 286 : and Lat. writers used
sigma of a
semicircular couch, Mart. 10.48.6 , etc.; cf. sigmoeidh/s. The rare form <*> is used in the numbering of building-stones in Berl.Sitzb. 1888.1234 , 1242 (Pergam.). From final s must be disting uished the character s =
6 , v. v v (sixth letter). the name si/gma ( si=gma) was usu. indeclinable, tou= si=gma
Pl.
l.c., Cra. 402e , 427a , Ath. 10.455c , Lyd. Mens. 1.21 ( v.l. si/gmatos ) ; tw=| si=gma
Gal. UP 2.14
, al.; tw=n si=gma
Pl.Com. 30
; ta\ si/gma ta\ e)pi\ tw=n a)spi/dwn
X. HG 4.4.10
, cf. Hellad. ap. Phot. Bibl. p.532
B. ; later declined, tou= si/gmatos
Eust. 1389.15
; si/gmasin
Id. 905.7
. we also hear of another name sa/n [a^], to/, ta\ ou)no/mata/ sfi (sc. toi=si *pe/rsh|si) teleutw=si pa/nta e)s tw)uto\ gra/mma, to\ *dwrie/es me\n sa\n kale/ousi, *)/iwnes de\ si/gma
Hdt. 1.139
, cf. Pi. Dith.Oxy. 1604
Fr. 1 ii 3 , Ath. 11.467a ; as name of the fourth and tenth letters in *qrasu/maxos, and of the sixth in *dionu/so(u), Epigr. ap. Ath. 10.454f , Achae. 33.4 ; cf. the compd. sam-fo/ras: sa/n and si/gma were evidently pronounced alike; it is conjectured that sa/n is originally the name of the old eighteenth letter.

cun- is very freq.; in Trag. both forms occur. The Prep. su/n gradually gave way to meta/ with gen., so that whereas A. has 67 examples of su/n to 8 of meta/ with gen., the proportions in Th. are 400 of meta/ to 37 of su/n, in D. 346 of meta/ to 15 of su/n, and in Arist. 300 of meta/ to 8 of su/n: for these and other statistics see C. J. T. Mommsen,
Beiträge zur Lehre von den griechischen Präpositionen (Frankfurt 1886 - 95 ): in Att. Prose and Com. su/n is restricted for the most part to signf. 8 , 9 and a few phrases, such as su\n qew=|, su\n (toi=s) o(/plois; Xenophon uses it freely, having 556 examples to 275 of meta/; in Pap., NT, and later Prose its use is much less restricted (v. infr.).
